solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Exclude start of Chinese poem that's meant to scan

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first of Chinese is used

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A rule about leaving out the opening of a Chinese poem whose metre must work properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scan' looks like the poetry sense (metre that works) but the definition is the supermarket sense: something made to be read by a scanner.
explanation.definitionFit: Striped product labels exist to be read by a checkout scanner, so this describes them.

clue.text: What I'm surprised to say you'll find in Sahara

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the word Sahara, read straight through

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise you might hear from a traveller in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection of sudden discovery or surprise, said when something dawns on you.

clue.text: Stick cold tongue that's chopped

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: chopping a word cuts off its end, so the last letter of the language word goes

parts.note: lingo is informal for a language or tongue

explanation.surface: A cold, cut-up tongue sticking together, perhaps in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to something is to adhere or grip tightly, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Old soldier who's had an up-and-down March

definitions.text: Old soldier who's had an up-and-down March

parts.words: Old soldier who's had an up-and-down March
parts.note: the nursery rhyme's grand old commander marched ten thousand men up to the top of the hill and down again

explanation.surface: A veteran who has had a mixed month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' is capitalised as the month but means a march of troops; the British nursery rhyme 'The Grand Old Duke of York' has him march his men up a hill and down again.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme nobleman is a commander famous only for marching his army up and down a hill.

clue.text: Smooth French author

definitions.meaning: to smooth wood by rubbing it with abrasive paper
George ... was the pen name of the 19th-century French novelist Aurore Dupin

explanation.definitionFit: One verb for rubbing a surface even with paper, and the pen name of a French novelist.

clue.text: Instructor drives a convertible

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driving teacher who motors around in a soft-top car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' poses as the car but is the signal to rearrange DRIVES and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who instructs gives guidance and counsel, as a consultant or mentor does.

clue.text: Arrow, silver, girl's got for old swordsman

parts.note: a dart is a small arrow
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Nan is a girl's name, short for Ann; the 's is read as 'has' with 'got'

explanation.surface: A list of weapons and treasure a girl has collected for an elderly fencer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gascon hero of Dumas's The Three Musketeers is a celebrated seventeenth-century swordsman.

clue.text: Nervous, finding money outside police station

indicators.note: the money word goes around the outside of the police word

parts.note: pay is money earned as wages
the nick is British slang for a police station

explanation.surface: Someone jittery on finding cash lying outside a police station.
explanation.walkthrough: THE NICK is British slang for a police station (or prison).
explanation.definitionFit: Being anxious and prone to sudden alarm is close in meaning to being nervous.

clue.text: Climber coming across gold material in tooth

indicators.note: the plant spreads across the metal, i.e. around it

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A climber who finds gold material inside a tooth, like a filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentine is the hard substance of teeth, and elephants' tusks are prized for it.

clue.text: In a hotdog, strangely head of gerbil is something lucky!

indicators.note: letters arranged strangely are put in an unexpected order
the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A surprised exclamation at finding a gerbil's head in a hotdog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns IN A HOTDOG into AGOODTHIN, and the G from gerbil is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortunate thing, an advantage or windfall: 'it's a fortunate state of affairs'.

clue.text: Shakespeare's first tragedy goes wrong: it's when he died

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
letters that go wrong fall out of order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's first tragedy flopping, and a note of the date he died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges TRAGEDY GOES behind the S. Shakespeare died on 23 April, England's patron saint's feast day.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is traditionally said to have both been born and died on 23 April, the feast of England's patron saint.

clue.text: Small cloak Billy maybe gives Aunt Sally

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a cape is a sleeveless cloak
a billy is a male goat, so a billy is one example

explanation.surface: Someone describing a small cloak that a man called Billy gives to his aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing at a figure, hence anyone set up as an easy target for blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean a person made the target of blame or criticism for others.

clue.text: Memorable problem: an unknown

parts.note: a catch is a hidden problem or snag
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A memorable maths problem involving one unknown quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that is instantly memorable sticks in the head, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Skipper in headgear can set about one

parts.note: a cap is a kind of headgear

indicators.note: the can word is set about, i.e. around, the single letter

parts.note: a tin is a can
a means one

explanation.surface: A ship's skipper in a hat, setting about opening a tin of food.
explanation.definitionFit: The skipper of a ship or team is its leader, the commanding officer.

clue.text: Bellowing after losing head, and rowing

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: roaring is bellowing loudly

explanation.surface: A coxswain yelling until hoarse, beheaded figuratively, and a crew rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Propelling a boat with oars is rowing; the word is an old synonym from the oar itself.

clue.text: Awful exponent of martial arts: a comic hero

parts.note: desperate can mean dreadful or awful
a dan is a grade of black belt in judo or karate, so a holder of one

explanation.surface: A terrible martial artist who is nonetheless a comic-book hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is the cow-pie-eating strongman of the British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The burly cowboy strongman is the long-running star of a British children's comic.

clue.text: Pull line, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: to draw a cart is to pull it

explanation.surface: Pull the line, so to speak, as an idiom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like the idiom meaning 'so to speak', but 'in' is the link and 'a manner of speaking' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow lazy way of talking with drawn-out vowels is a particular manner of speech.

clue.text: Very old colonel, awfully loud, first of all outspoken

indicators.note: takes the first letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A very old colonel, terribly loud and frank above everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Being outspoken means expressing views freely and forcefully, as a vocal critic does.

clue.text: Composer in short video — one embracing girl

indicators.note: the video-and-one letters wrap around the girl's name

parts.note: vid is a short form of video
Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A composer appearing in a brief video where someone hugs a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian baroque composer of The Four Seasons.

clue.text: Little girl not seen in Asia's capitals

definitions.meaning: a name for a girl, short for Dorothy, and also something tiny
the small mark over a lower-case i disappears when the word Asia is written in capital letters

explanation.definitionFit: A pet name for Dorothy, and the small point over a lower-case i that capital letters lack.

clue.text: Minister's offer spurned by Queen

indicators.note: the queen letters are rejected and thrown out of the offer word

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer, as for a contract
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's queen

explanation.surface: A government minister's proposal turned down by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in to minister to the sick; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To minister to someone is to look after or care for them, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Gaily, it moves, displaying this?

indicators.note: letters that move shift position into a new order

explanation.surface: Something moving merrily shows nimbleness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges GAILY and IT; the whole clue is also the definition, as something moving gaily shows nimbleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbleness and quickness of movement is what a gaily moving thing displays.
